proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, proof of Lemma 1.3 (p. 207), for a single β = β_j ∈ 𝒦⁺. The printed text reads: "By the XXX Theorem 3.23 of Ch. 1 we know that (since there is a Radon measure γ_j on ℝ^{n+ℓ} characterized by γ_j(B) = ∫_{Gₙ(B)} β_j(S) dV(y,S) for Borel sets B ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}) (1) e(x,j) = lim_{ρ↓0} ∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β_j(S) dV(y,S) / μ_V(B_ρ(x)) exists for each x ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} ∖ Z_j, where Z_j is a Borel set with μ_V(Z_j) = 0 and e(x,j) is a μ_V-measurable function of x, with (2) ∫_A e(x,j) dμ_V(x) = ∫_{Gₙ(A)} β_j(S) dV(y,S) for any Borel set A." Correction (a) of the parent proof is applied: μ_V is only Radon on the open set U, not necessarily locally finite at ∂U, so the differentiation theorem is applied on U, where both measures are Radon.

Notation. G := G(N,n), a compact space. μ := μ_V = V.weight, so μ(A) = V(A × G) for Borel A (Varifold.weight_apply). c := sup_G |β| = ‖β‖ < ∞, so 0 ≤ β(S) ≤ c for all S. We use three facts:
(F1) μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = V((ℝ^N∖U) × G) = 0 (field V.supported);
(F2) μ(K) = V(K × G) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact);
(F3) μ is σ-finite (instance Varifold.weight.instSigmaFinite).

1. The measure γ (the printed γ_j). Let F(y,S) := ofReal(β(S)) ∈ [0,∞), a Borel function on ℝ^N × G. Put γ := π_#(V⌞F) with π(y,S) = y, i.e. γ := (V.measure.withDensity F).map Prod.fst. For Borel B ⊆ ℝ^N we have π⁻¹(B) = B × G, so γ(B) = ∫⁻_{B×G} ofReal(β(S)) dV(y,S) (Measure.map_apply, withDensity_apply, Set.prod_univ).

2. Comparison with μ. For Borel B, ofReal(β(S)) ≤ ofReal(c) gives γ(B) ≤ ofReal(c)·V(B × G) = ofReal(c)·μ(B) (lintegral_mono, setLIntegral_const). Hence γ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0 by (F1), and γ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U by (F2). Also γ ≪ μ, since μ(B) = 0 forces γ(B) = 0 for Borel B (Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.mk).

3. γ is the zero extension of a Radon measure on U. Let γ_U := γ.comap Subtype.val be the restriction of γ to the open subspace U, so γ_U(C) = γ(C) for Borel C ⊆ U.
(a) γ_U.map Subtype.val = γ⌞U = γ, because γ(ℝ^N∖U) = 0 (map_comap_subtype_coe, Measure.restrict_eq_self_of_ae_mem).
(b) γ_U is locally finite. U is an open subset of ℝ^N, hence locally compact (IsOpen.locallyCompactSpace), so each y ∈ U has a compact neighbourhood C in U (exists_compact_mem_nhds). Its image in ℝ^N is a compact subset of U, so γ_U(C) = γ(C) < ∞ by step 2.
(c) γ is σ-finite: it is the push-forward of the locally finite, hence σ-finite, measure γ_U on the second-countable space U under the measurable embedding Subtype.val (MeasurableEmbedding.sigmaFinite_map).

4. Differentiation (printed (1); Ch. 1, 3.23(i)). Apply the Besicovitch differentiation theorem on the open set U to the Radon measures γ_U and μ_U := V.domainWeight. Every satellite configuration in the metric subspace U is also one in ℝ^N, so U has the Besicovitch covering property, and closed balls of U are traces of closed balls of ℝ^N. Transporting back along the inclusion, using γ_U.map val = γ and μ_U.map val = μ, gives: for μ-a.e. x,
 γ(B_ρ(x)) / μ(B_ρ(x)) → g(x) := (dγ/dμ)(x) in [0,∞] as ρ ↓ 0,
 where dγ/dμ = γ.rnDeriv μ and the quotients are in [0,∞] with a/b = a·b⁻¹.
 This is exactly the kernel-checked SimonGMT lemma Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.Varifold.ae_tendsto_firstVariationDensity_of_domainMeasure V γ_U (FirstVariationDensity.lean:60; it uses hasBesicovitchCovering_subtype, :30). It is in the import closure of GMT.Ch08.Submission and uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. After rewriting γ_U.map Subtype.val = γ by 3(a), its conclusion reads: ∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Tendsto (fun r ↦ γ (closedBall x r) / V.weight (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (γ.rnDeriv V.weight x)).
 Mathematically equivalent route (supplied detail (a)): apply Besicovitch's theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv) to the finite measures γ⌞K and μ⌞K for compact K ⊆ U, at points of interior K, where small closed balls lie in K. Identify d(γ⌞K)/d(μ⌞K) = dγ/dμ μ⌞K-a.e. by uniqueness of the Lebesgue decomposition (Measure.eq_rnDeriv), and use countably many such K whose interiors cover U.
 Moreover g(x) < ∞ for μ-a.e. x, since γ is σ-finite (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top). Define e(x) := g(x).toReal ∈ [0,∞). Then e is Borel measurable (Measure.measurable_rnDeriv, Measurable.ennreal_toReal).

5. The real quotient: proof of (1). By step 4 and (F1), μ-a.e. x satisfies three conditions at once: x ∈ U, γ(B_ρ(x))/μ(B_ρ(x)) → g(x), and g(x) < ∞. Fix such an x and choose r > 0 with ball(x,r) ⊆ U.
 Let 0 < ρ < r and B := B_ρ(x). Then B ⊆ ball(x,r) ⊆ U is compact, so μ(B) = V(B × G) < ∞ by (F2). The function z ↦ β(z.2) is continuous, ≥ 0 and bounded by c, hence integrable on B × G for V (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). Therefore
 γ(B) = ∫⁻_{B×G} ofReal(β(z.2)) dV = ofReal(∫_{B×G} β(z.2) dV) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal),
 and since the integral is ≥ 0, γ(B).toReal = ∫_{B×G} β(z.2) dV (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). Because (a/b).toReal = a.toReal / b.toReal for all a, b ∈ [0,∞] (ENNReal.toReal_div), for every ρ ∈ (0, r):
 (∫_{B_ρ(x)×G} β(z.2) dV) / μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal = (γ(B_ρ(x)) / μ(B_ρ(x))).toReal.
 Since g(x) ≠ ∞ and toReal is continuous at finite points (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), (γ(B_ρ(x))/μ(B_ρ(x))).toReal → g(x).toReal = e(x) as ρ ↓ 0. Since (0, r) ∈ 𝓝[>]0, the real quotient has the same limit (Tendsto.congr'). This proves (1).

6. The integral identity: proof of (2). γ ≪ μ by step 2, and γ, μ are σ-finite by 3(c) and (F3). The Radon–Nikodym theorem gives μ⌞g = γ (Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_eq), i.e. γ(A) = ∫⁻_A g dμ for every Borel A (withDensity_apply). Since g < ∞ μ-a.e., g(x) = ofReal(g(x).toReal) = ofReal(e(x)) for μ-a.e. x (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). Hence ∫⁻_A g dμ = ∫⁻_A ofReal(e) dμ (setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae). With step 1, ∫⁻_{A×G} ofReal(β(S)) dV = γ(A) = ∫⁻_A ofReal(e(x)) dμ(x). This is (2), the printed (2) written as an identity of lintegrals. ∎
key_steps: γ(B) := ∫⁻_{B×G} ofReal β dV is the Borel measure π_#(V⌞ofReal∘β∘snd) on ℝ^N with γ ≤ ‖β‖·μ_V; hence γ vanishes off U, is finite on compact subsets of U, and γ ≪ μ_V.
γ is the zero extension of the locally finite measure γ.comap Subtype.val on U, hence σ-finite.
Besicovitch differentiation on U (SimonGMT Varifold.ae_tendsto_firstVariationDensity_of_domainMeasure): γ(B_ρ(x))/μ_V(B_ρ(x)) → dγ/dμ_V(x) < ∞ for μ_V-a.e. x; set e := toReal(dγ/dμ_V).
For x ∈ U and small ρ, the real Bochner quotient equals toReal of the [0,∞] ratio (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, ENNReal.toReal_div); this gives (1).
Radon–Nikodym gives μ_V⌞(dγ/dμ_V) = γ, and dγ/dμ_V = ofReal∘e μ_V-a.e.; this gives (2).
